hafm-01-c2.text: Cesar A. Fortes-Lima, Concetta Burgarella, Rickard Hammarén, et al (2024). The genetic legacy of the expansion of Bantu-speaking peoples in Africa. Nature 625(7995): 540-547 (epub Nov 2023).
hafm-01-c2.quote: this expansion that started 6,000-4,000 years ago in western Africa.
hafm-01-c2.claim: A 2024 study in Nature led by Cesar Fortes-Lima, which sampled more than 1,500 Bantu speakers, dates the start of the expansion to roughly 6,000 to 4,000 years ago in western Africa.

hafm-04-c2.text: Mark Cartwright (2019). Timbuktu: West Africa's Great Trading Centre. World History Encyclopedia.
hafm-04-c2.quote: Mansa Musa I was the ruler of the Mali Empire in West Africa from 1312 to 1337.
hafm-04-c2.claim: Mansa Musa ruled Mali from about 1312 to 1337; the dates are uncertain.

hafm-05-c1.text: Mark Cartwright (2019). Kilwa. World History Encyclopedia.
hafm-05-c1.quote: Ibn Battuta (1304 - c. 1368 CE), who visited c. 1331 CE, to famously describe Kilwa as "one of the most beautiful towns in the world"
hafm-05-c1.claim: Ibn Battuta, visiting about 1331, called Kilwa one of the most beautiful and best-built towns in the world.

hafm-02-c1.text: Joshua J. Mark (2018). The Kingdom of Kush. World History Encyclopedia.
hafm-02-c1.quote: The end of the Kerma period is usually given as c. 1500 BCE when Thutmose I attacked the city.
hafm-02-c1.claim: Egyptian armies under Thutmose I destroyed it around 1500 BCE.

hafm-02-c1.text: Joshua J. Mark (2018). The Kingdom of Kush. World History Encyclopedia.
hafm-02-c1.quote: Piye did not negotiate with those he saw as rebel princes and marched his army north, conquering all the cities of Lower Egypt, and then returned to Napata.
hafm-02-c1.claim: Around 728 BCE King Piye marched north and conquered Egypt

hafm-02-c3.text: Mark Cartwright (2019). Kingdom of Axum. World History Encyclopedia.
hafm-02-c3.quote: The gold and silver coins of Axum, which appeared from the 3rd century CE onwards, have Greek inscriptions, Sabaean religious symbols, and they were minted adhering to Roman standard weights.
hafm-02-c3.claim: From around 270 CE, under King Endubis, Aksum minted its own coins in gold, silver and bronze, a rare step then; gold coins carried Greek legends.

hafm-03-c1.text: Mark Cartwright (2019). Ghana Empire. World History Encyclopedia.
hafm-03-c1.quote: Control of regional trade was a lucrative business for the kings of Ghana who passed on goods like gold, ivory, hides, ostrich feathers, and slaves to the Muslim merchants (particularly the Sanhaja Berbers) who sent camel caravans that crossed the Sahara from North Africa and which brought much-valued salt to the south.
hafm-03-c1.claim: The savanna and forest zones of West Africa had gold but little salt; the Sahara had salt but needed grain; North Africa and the Mediterranean wanted gold for coinage.

hafm-03-c2.text: Mark Cartwright (2019). Ghana Empire. World History Encyclopedia.
hafm-03-c2.quote: The king did rely on advisors and, from the 11th century, even recruited Muslim merchants to act as interpreters and as officials who helped manage the economy and keep track of the goods coming in and out of the country.
hafm-03-c2.claim: The king, Tunka Manin in 1063, followed the local religion but employed Muslim ministers and interpreters.

hafm-03-c3.text: Mark Cartwright (2019). Ghana Empire. World History Encyclopedia.
hafm-03-c3.quote: The Ghana Empire struggled to recover thereafter; Muslim rulers may have been imposed by the Almoravids but concrete evidence is lacking for any sort of conquest.
hafm-03-c3.claim: No contemporary source describes a military conquest

hafm-06-c1.text: Mark Cartwright (2019). Ife. World History Encyclopedia.
hafm-06-c1.quote: The Yoruba considered the site of Ife the exact place of creation, that is where the gods descended from heaven and created the world as we know it.
hafm-06-c1.claim: Ile-Ife, in southwestern Nigeria, is the sacred city where, in Yoruba tradition, the world was created and the first king, Oduduwa, ruled.

hafm-06-c3.text: Mark Cartwright (2019). Kingdom of Kongo. World History Encyclopedia.
hafm-06-c3.quote: Catholicism was established as the official religion of the royal household, the capital was renamed Sao Salvador, churches were built, and Affonso even successfully invited the Pope to permit the appointment of a Kongo bishop.
hafm-06-c3.claim: His son Mvemba a Nzinga, who ruled as Afonso I from about 1509 to 1542, made Catholicism a royal religion, founded schools and wrote to Lisbon in Portuguese.
